reference: GNU patch 2.8 (and GNU diffutils diff for the round trip), compared for stdout, status and the resulting files, including .orig and .rej.
coverage: Guest pass 3 G45: fuzz is capped at the hunk's context, so deleted lines must match; zero- and one-line-context hunks fail rather than overwrite.
Ordinary fuzz on a context line, and diff -ruN | patch -p1 creating and removing files.
exclusions: Interactive questions on a terminal and context-format (diff -c) patches are outside this suite.

cases.purpose: G45: a zero-context hunk whose '-' line does not match fails (no fuzz is possible without context): Hunk FAILED, f.rej and f.orig written, file unchanged, status 1.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
DIFFERENT
four
five
' > f
printf -- '--- f
+++ f
@@ -3 +3 @@
-three
+THREE
' > p0
patch f < p0 || echo rc=$?
cat f f.rej

cases.purpose: G45: a one-line hunk -a +b on a file holding z fails instead of overwriting it.
cases.script:
echo z > s
printf -- '--- s
+++ s
@@ -1 +1 @@
-a
+b
' > p1
patch s < p1 || echo rc=$?
cat s

cases.purpose: G45: fuzz still ignores an outer context line: a differing context line applies 'with fuzz 1', status 0.
cases.script:
printf '1
2
3
X
old
Y
7
8
' > h
printf -- '--- h
+++ h
@@ -4,3 +4,3 @@
 x
-old
+new
 y
' > p
patch h < p || echo rc=$?
cat h

cases.purpose: G45: with one line of context on each side, fuzz 1 drops only the context; a '-' line that differs still fails.
cases.script:
printf '1
2
3
X
OLDX
Y
7
8
' > h
printf -- '--- h
+++ h
@@ -4,3 +4,3 @@
 x
-old
+new
 y
' > p
patch h < p || echo rc=$?
cat h

cases.purpose: G45: a default three-line-context hunk with a mismatched '-' line fails at every fuzz level.
cases.script:
printf 'a
b
c
WRONG
e
f
g
' > t
printf -- '--- t
+++ t
@@ -1,7 +1,7 @@
 a
 b
 c
-d
+D
 e
 f
 g
' > p
patch t < p || echo rc=$?
cat t

cases.purpose: G45/G46: a diff -ruN patch applied with patch -p1 recreates the new tree: changed, created and deleted (Epoch-dated, now empty) files; the deleted file is removed.
cases.script:
export TZ=UTC
mkdir -p a/sub b/sub b/onlyb
printf '1\n2\n' > a/x
printf '1\nTWO\n' > b/x
echo o > a/sub/old
echo k > a/sub/keep
echo K > b/sub/keep
echo n > b/onlyb/new
diff -ruN a b > fix.patch || echo diff-rc=$?
cp -r a work
cd work
patch -p1 < ../fix.patch || echo rc=$?
cd ..
rm -r a
rm fix.patch
